column1: # PARAM.SFO — the title metadata table, as two independent open-source projects read and
# write it.
# Columns: struct, field, offset, size, type, value, note
# read-from: pfd_sfo_tools@vendored      sfopatcher/src/sfo.{c,h}     C       READER + WRITER
#            ps5upload@vendored          engine/crates/ps5upload-pkg  Rust    reader + writer
# Both sides of the format are covered twice, which is unusual for anything in this
# repository and worth stating: the container needed four sources before a writer turned up,
# and the package still has none. Here the first source found was a writer.
# The two agree on every field. They were written years apart in different languages, so the
# agreement is evidence rather than a shared assumption.
# # Where the sources were wrong, and eleven files said so
# The C writer pads the key table so the **whole file** is a multiple of sixteen. No real file
# does this. Eleven were checked — three PS5 packages, two PS4 toolchain samples, and six PS3
# titles and saves — and every one pads the **key table to a multiple of four** and ends
# exactly where its last value ends.
# All eleven now round-trip byte for byte. The layout rows below are the measured rule, not
# the cited one; the cited one is recorded here so it cannot be re-read and re-believed.
# (D019, principle 2)
# **No vendor binary was read to produce this table.** Real files in `titles/` are used to
# confirm rows, never to derive them. (principle 2)
# # The version, and why it is two bytes rather than a number
# Both sources write `01 01 00 00` and call it 1.1. A reader that treats it as the integer
# 0x00000101 gets the same bytes; one that treats it as 0x0101 and writes it back as a u16
# does not. Recorded as the four bytes it is.
# # PS5 versus PS4
# The structure is generation-independent — the same twenty-byte header and sixteen-byte
# index entries appear in packages for both consoles. What differs is the *keys*, and keys
# are content rather than format, so they are not in this table. The current generation also
# carries `param.json` alongside or instead; see the `param` module.
